#### Quadratic/Quadratic Rational Function Model {#sec-pmd-644}

[**Q/Q Rational Function Model Starting Values**]{#sec-pmd-644-starting}

Based on the procedure described in [4.6.4.2](#sec-pmd-642-starting), we fit the model:

$$y = A_0 + A_1 x + A_2 x^2 - B_1 x - B_2 x^2 + \varepsilon \, ,$$

using the following five representative points to generate the starting values for the Q/Q rational function.

| Temp | THERMEXP |
|---:|---:|
| 10 | 0 |
| 50 | 5 |
| 120 | 12 |
| 200 | 15 |
| 800 | 20 |

The coefficients from the preliminary linear fit of the five points are:

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
x <- c(10, 50, 120, 200, 800)
y <- c(0, 5, 12, 15, 20)
x2 <- x * x
xy <- -x * y
x2y <- -(x * x * y)

start_fit_qq <- lm(y ~ x + x2 + xy + x2y)
coef(start_fit_qq)
```

[**Nonlinear Fit Results**]{#sec-pmd-644-fit}

The results for the nonlinear fit are shown below.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| message: false
hahn <- read_table(
  here::here("datasets", "HAHN1.DAT"),
  skip = 25,
  col_names = c("temperature", "thermal_expansion")
)

stc <- coef(start_fit_qq)

fit_qq <- nls(
  thermal_expansion ~ (a0 + a1 * temperature + a2 * temperature^2) /
    (1 + b1 * temperature + b2 * temperature^2),
  data = hahn,
  start = list(a0 = stc[1], a1 = stc[2], a2 = stc[3], b1 = stc[4], b2 = stc[5])
)

summary(fit_qq)
```

The regression yields the following estimated model.

$$\hat y = \frac{-8.028 + 0.508x - 0.007307x^2}{1 - 0.00704x - 0.0003288x^2}$$

[**Plot of Q/Q Rational Function Fit**]{#sec-pmd-644-predicted}

We generate a plot of the fitted rational function model with the raw data.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| label: fig-pmd-644-overlay
#| fig-cap: "Thermal expansion of copper data overlaid with the Q/Q rational function fit"
hahn <- hahn |> mutate(residual_qq = resid(fit_qq), fitted_qq = fitted(fit_qq))

ggplot(hahn, aes(temperature, thermal_expansion)) +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(aes(y = fitted_qq), color = "firebrick") +
  labs(x = "Temperature (K)", y = "Coefficient of Thermal Expansion") +
  theme_light()
```

Looking at the fitted function with the raw data appears to show a reasonable fit.

[**6-Plot for Model Validation**]{#sec-pmd-644-6plot}

Although the plot of the fitted function with the raw data appears to show a reasonable fit, we need to validate the [model assumptions](#sec-pmd-21). The 6-plot<!-- XREF: EDA section 3.3, Graphical Techniques: Alphabetic, 6-Plot; source handbook/eda/section3/6plot.htm --> is an effective tool for this purpose.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| warning: false
#| label: fig-pmd-644-6plot
#| fig-cap: "6-plot for the Q/Q rational function fit"
library(patchwork)

six_plot <- function(x, y, residual, fitted) {
  d <- tibble(x = x, y = y, residual = residual, fitted = fitted) |>
    mutate(lag_residual = lag(residual))

  p1 <- ggplot(d, aes(x, y)) +
    geom_point(color = "steelblue") +
    geom_line(aes(y = fitted), color = "firebrick") +
    labs(x = "Temperature (K)", y = "Coefficient of Thermal Expansion", title = "Data with Fit") +
    theme_light()

  p2 <- ggplot(d, aes(x, residual)) +
    geom_point(color = "steelblue") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
    labs(x = "Temperature (K)", y = "Residual", title = "Residuals vs Temperature") +
    theme_light()

  p3 <- ggplot(d, aes(fitted, residual)) +
    geom_point(color = "steelblue") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
    labs(x = "Predicted", y = "Residual", title = "Residuals vs Predicted") +
    theme_light()

  p4 <- ggplot(d, aes(lag_residual, residual)) +
    geom_point(color = "steelblue") +
    labs(x = "Residual[i-1]", y = "Residual[i]", title = "Lag Plot") +
    theme_light()

  p5 <- ggplot(d, aes(residual)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 15, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.6, color = "white") +
    labs(x = "Residual", y = "Count", title = "Histogram") +
    theme_light()

  p6 <- ggplot(d, aes(sample = residual)) +
    stat_qq(color = "steelblue") +
    stat_qq_line(color = "firebrick") +
    labs(x = "Theoretical Quantiles", y = "Residual", title = "Normal Probability Plot") +
    theme_light()

  (p1 + p2 + p3) / (p4 + p5 + p6)
}

six_plot(hahn$temperature, hahn$thermal_expansion, hahn$residual_qq, hahn$fitted_qq)
```

The plot of the residuals versus the predictor variable temperature (row 1, column 2) and of the residuals versus the predicted values (row 1, column 3) indicate a distinct pattern in the residuals. This suggests that the assumption of random errors is badly violated.

[**Residual Plot**]{#sec-pmd-644-residuals}

We generate a full-sized residual plot in order to show more detail.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| label: fig-pmd-644-residuals
#| fig-cap: "Residuals from the Q/Q rational function fit versus temperature"
ggplot(hahn, aes(temperature, residual_qq)) +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  labs(x = "Temperature (K)", y = "Residuals") +
  theme_light()
```

The full-sized residual plot clearly shows the distinct pattern in the residuals. When residuals exhibit a clear pattern, the corresponding errors are probably not random.
